title: Architect: file structure for a static site
when: The architect sets up where files live for a static site or small web app before the developers start writing.
prompt:
Goal: A flat, obvious layout that opens from index.html with relative paths and gives every file one clear job.
Steps:
1. Run list_files and keep what exists; never move user files without a reason written in a note.
2. Keep pages at the root (index.html, about.html) so links stay relative and short.
3. Use at most three folders: css/ for styles, js/ for modules, assets/ for images and data; skip folders a two file project does not need.
4. Name files by role in lowercase with hyphens: js/cart.js, js/storage.js, assets/menu.json.
5. Plan one entry script per page loaded with type="module", importing the others with ./ paths.
6. Write STRUCTURE.md: a tree of the files and one line per file saying what it holds and who owns it.
Quality bar:
- Every path works when index.html is opened from disk.
- No file does two unrelated jobs.
- The tree fits on one screen.
Pitfalls:
- Absolute paths (/css/style.css) that break when opened from a folder.
- Deep nesting such as src/app/components/ui for six files.
- Module scripts that need a server without saying so in the README.
Verify:
- [ ] STRUCTURE.md starts with a # heading and lists every file.
- [ ] All planned paths are relative.
- [ ] At most three folders.
- [ ] Each file has an owner.
Output: STRUCTURE.md with the tree and per file purpose; empty folders are not created.

examples.input: organiza a estrutura do site da escola
examples.output: index.html, cursos.html, css/style.css, js/main.js, assets/cursos.json, plus STRUCTURE.md
